themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it. So the models start small: build a few cases they can actually prove, then grade everything else against that.
themes.evidence: Today's answers on cross-channel incrementality all say platform bidding shifts during the test, echoing answer engine optimization (no stable baseline), identity resolution (no truth set for who is the same person), and B2B buying-group signal loss (outcomes arrive quarters late).

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a picture next to a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, what a message is worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement usually has budget attached.
themes.evidence: Generative content governance keeps running into implied claims that no registry holds, the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions a political fight rather than a modeling gap, and journey orchestration answers say nobody can agree what a message is worth.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every model answering safe agent execution proposes a proxy or gateway with hard spend and audience caps, and the same pattern shows up as a single egress checkpoint in downstream consent enforcement and a shared contact ledger every channel must check in journey orchestration.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a dollar, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from the outside: expiring lists, planted test records, and judging spend by your own sales data.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent answers describe ad platforms and trained models as one-way traps that cannot unlearn a person, and the ad supply integrity and incrementality answers both fall back on judging platforms against outcomes observed in first-party records.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by handing it over, and nobody can force them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers keep proposing a faster declared-agent lane because agents profit by passing as human, identity resolution answers say platform owners profit from broken links, and incrementality answers note platforms control both the treatment and the evidence.
